subject: AxiomCore — Quantization swap causing latency & hallucination uptick
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@axiomcore.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency + hallucination spike after nightly model swap

Hi Rachel,

Quick heads-up — our traffic started spiking in latency and error rate around 02:30 UTC this morning right after the scheduled model upgrade (v3.2 -> v3.3 with "photon-quant-v2" profile). Key symptoms: p95 CPU-side latency jumped from ~420ms to ~1.2s, a ~3x increase; token decode errors and a rise in hallucination-like completions on long contexts (>512 tokens).

We rolled a small canary at 01:45 and then the full switch at 02:00. We have attached a sampling of erroneous outputs and some perf traces. Our production SLOs are being violated and the support queue is filling. Customers are already complaining.

Can your team please:
- Immediately advise if you can rollback to the previous quant profile?
- If rollback isn't possible, do you have a safe mitigation (disable batching / reduce max tokens) we can apply from our side?
- ETA for a fix or detailed triage steps we should expect?

This is high priority for us — CC'ing our procurement and CTO as requested by legal for follow-up on credits if needed.

Thanks,
Sara Li
Customer Success Lead, AxiomCore
Attachments: error_samples_0614.txt, perf_dump_0614.json

From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@axiomcore.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + hallucination spike after nightly model swap

Sara — thanks for the quick signal and the artifacts. We're treating this with priority.

Immediate plan:
1) I'm authorizing an emergency rollback of the quant profile to the pre-upgrade variant (photon-quant-v1) if Karthik confirms it will restore baseline.
2) If rollback could cause compatibility issues with the v3.3 weights, we'll instead temporarily disable cross-request batching and reduce max_response_tokens to 400 for affected routes as a mitigation.
3) We'll open an incident Slack channel and do a 30-min war room; I'll be on the call.

Karthik / Mina — please triage and confirm whether rollback is safe, expected impact, and the steps. Please attach any JVM/GPU traces and a short checklist for our ops runbook.

I'll follow up with Sara with a timeline within 30 minutes.

— Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@axiomcore.com>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + hallucination spike after nightly model swap

On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 9:05 AM Sara Li <sara.li@axiomcore.com> wrote:
> Quick heads-up — our traffic started spiking in latency and error rate around 02:30 UTC this morning after the scheduled model upgrade (v3.2 -> v3.3 with "photon-quant-v2" profile).

Triage summary (initial):
- Observed a p95 jump coincident with the qprofile flip. Error-rate (5xx) from decoder increased from 0.2% -> 1.8%.
- Root candidate: photon-quant-v2 changes per-token kernel tiling and reorders KV-cache entries for attention heads that cross the 512-token boundary. For sequences >512 tokens we see decode stalls and occasional token misalignment that can look like hallucinations.
- Canary logs show the same pattern on our canaries; it's reproducible with the v3.3 weights + photon-quant-v2.

Immediate ops recommendations:
A) Rollback qprofile to photon-quant-v1 (expected restore of prior perf). Risk: small change in memory footprint; we need to monitor OOMs during rollback but probability low given canary baseline.
B) If you prefer not to rollback now: set max_tokens=400 and set batching.window_ms=0 (disable cross-request batching) — both reduce likelihood of stalls but increase per-token cost.
C) Schedule fast patch: fix KV-cache alignment in kernel (low-level runtime fix). ETA for dev -> canary -> prod ~48-72 hours under priority.

I attached a perf dump + quick grep of decoder logs (perf_dump_0614.json). If you want us to proceed with rollback now, say the word and we'll run the plan: 1) pin traffic for 5 minutes, 2) apply qprofile revert, 3) observe metrics for 15 minutes, 4) full roll back if stable.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Li <sara.li@axiomcore.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurements@axiomcore.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@axiomcore.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency + hallucination spike after nightly model swap

Rachel / Karthik — thank you for the quick triage. We want the fastest route to stable SLOs. Please proceed with rollback now and run the observe window.

Two asks from us:
- Please confirm the rollback window and expected customer-visible downtime (we need wording for our status page).
- Procurement will follow up on SLA credits if the incident breaches monthly SLOs.

Michael (CTO) — looping you in; please advise if you want us to pause any downstream batch jobs that rely on >512 token contexts while this is resolved.

Sara Li
Customer Success Lead, AxiomCore

From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@axiomcore.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@axiomcore.com>, Procurement <procurements@axiomcore.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:31:00 -0700
Subject: Incident wrap + exec summary: rollback completed, next steps

Sara / Michael — quick summary for execs and procurement:
- What happened: A scheduled model rollout included a new quantization profile (photon-quant-v2) that changes KV-cache ordering. For long-context requests (>512 tokens) this caused decode stalls and token misalignment, raising p95 latency and apparent hallucinations.
- Action taken: At 11:20 PDT on 2027-06-14 we initiated an emergency rollback to photon-quant-v1 across AxiomCore's production allocation. Observed metrics returned to baseline within the 15-minute observe window. No customer-visible downtime beyond transient increased latency during the immediate rollback window.
- Current status: Stable on photon-quant-v1. We've limited cross-request batching on a small subset of routes for additional safety.
- Next steps / owners:
  * Karthik: kernel-level fix for KV-cache alignment (ETA 48–72h).
  * Mina: coordinate extended canary and test matrix (long-context, batched workloads).
  * Rachel: post-mortem and exec write-up; will schedule a review with AxiomCore executives.

Procurement note: we'll provide incident timing and metrics for your SLA review. We'll also propose a one-time service credit if the incident meets Redwood's SLA breach criteria; Rachel and our finance ops will coordinate.

I'll open a post-mortem doc and share the link (SUP-6129). Thanks for the swift partnership and patience — we'll follow up with the post-mortem and a plan to prevent regressions during quant profile upgrades.

— Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachments: deployment_plan_diffs.pdf
